t1.text: Top level — front door, model, use cases, index, training, registry

t2.text: One use case, seven uncramped screens — left rail

t3.text: Workbench and operations — prompts, datasets, alerts, usage, unregistered

n1.text: Sketch v3 (2026-11-02). Numbers shown are the ones the Head of ThinkLatent stated; everything else is a placeholder or an illustrative shape until the telemetry contract (TL-009), the training pipeline and the index feed the pages. Press Play on any screen: links walk the journey. Engineering view reveals lineage and the trace.

n2.text: v3 adds what the five scout briefs found: latency by request shape with p50·p99 and a TTFT split; goodput, error budget and saturation; acceptance and persistence as the quality headline; judge calibration before any judge number; Official vs Practice runs with intervals; a record that is the single governed object; prompts as releases; datasets with lineage; alerts from thresholds plus a weekly digest; usage with forecasts; and the side door made visible.

t5.text: v4 (2026-11-05) — Home by role, playground, agents, model card, release, lineage

t6.text: v4 — project, data review and insight, evaluation, help, operations, core team

n3.text: Sketch v4 (2026-11-05) builds decision 9 and the 2026-11-05 dictation: a dock of ten areas (Home, Models, Agents, Playground, Evaluation, Projects, Data, Training, Operations, Help); Home changes by role; the project is the unit of membership, budget and data with phases POC → Build → Pilot in production → Production; production is sealed (break-glass only), aggregate open and drill-in gated; agents replace blueprints; evaluation results, index, leaderboard and corrections live in the portal; the core-team view carries the Claude Code bridge and the AI guide. Older v3 pages (top rows) keep their content and will take the dock in v4.1.
